competitive.patchTrend: Amumu needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
competitive.metaEvolution: Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Bandage Toss is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Amumu's jungle pressure.
Use Despair as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Tantrum or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Conqueror is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Amumu does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Bandage Toss and Tantrum only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Curse of the Sad Mummy should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 125 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Amumu can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Amumu's passive, Cursed Touch, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Amumu cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Curse of the Sad Mummy sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Amumu wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Amumu tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Amumu should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Amumu wants to fight from.
If 53 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Amumu's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Amumu can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Heartsteel -> Sunfire Aegis -> Jak'Sho, The Protean is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Amumu's teamfight rating is 53/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Amumu should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Amumu, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Amumu needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Amumu's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Amumu's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.name: Anivia
champions.title: the Cryophoenix
champions.blurb: Anivia is a benevolent winged spirit who endures endless cycles of life, death, and rebirth to protect the Freljord. A demigod born of unforgiving ice and bitter winds, she wields those elemental powers to thwart any who dare disturb her homeland...
champions.lore: Anivia is a benevolent winged spirit who endures endless cycles of life, death, and rebirth to protect the Freljord. A demigod born of unforgiving ice and bitter winds, she wields those elemental powers to thwart any who dare disturb her homeland. Anivia guides and protects the tribes of the harsh north, who revere her as a symbol of hope, and a portent of great change. She fights with every ounce of her being, knowing that through her sacrifice, her memory will endure, and she will be reborn into a new tomorrow.

abilities.name: Rebirth
abilities.description: Upon taking fatal damage, Anivia reverts to an egg and is reborn with full health.

abilities.name: Flash Frost
abilities.description: Anivia brings her wings together and summons a sphere of ice that flies towards her opponents, chilling and damaging anyone in its path. When the sphere explodes it does moderate damage in a radius, stunning anyone in the area.

abilities.name: Crystallize

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Flash Frost is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Anivia's mid pressure.
Use Crystallize as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Frostbite or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Arcane Comet is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Anivia does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Flash Frost and Frostbite only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Glacial Storm should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 600 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Anivia can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Anivia's passive, Rebirth, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Anivia cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Glacial Storm sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Anivia wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Anivia tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Anivia should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Anivia wants to fight from.
If 51 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Anivia's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Anivia can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Stormsurge -> Rabadon's Deathcap is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Anivia's teamfight rating is 54/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Anivia should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Anivia, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Anivia needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Anivia's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Anivia's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.lore: Dangerous, yet disarmingly precocious, Annie is a child mage with immense pyromantic power. Even in the shadows of the mountains north of Noxus, she is a magical outlier. Her natural affinity for fire manifested early in life through unpredictable, emotional outbursts, though she eventually learned to control these “playful tricks.” Her favorite includes the summoning of her beloved teddy bear, Tibbers, as a fiery protector. Lost in the perpetual innocence of childhood, Annie wanders the dark forests, always looking for someone to play with.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Disintegrate is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Annie's mid pressure.
Use Incinerate as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Molten Shield or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Arcane Comet is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Annie does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Disintegrate and Molten Shield only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Summon: Tibbers should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 625 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Annie can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Annie's passive, Pyromania, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Annie cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Summon: Tibbers sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Annie wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Annie tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Annie should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Annie wants to fight from.
If 50 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Annie's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Annie can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Stormsurge -> Rabadon's Deathcap is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Annie's teamfight rating is 55/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Annie should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Annie, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Annie needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Annie's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Annie's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.title: the Weapon of the Faithful
champions.blurb: Emerging from moonlight's shadow with weapons drawn, Aphelios kills the enemies of his faith in brooding silence—speaking only through the certainty of his aim, and the firing of each gun. Though fueled by a poison that renders him mute, he is guided by...
champions.lore: Emerging from moonlight's shadow with weapons drawn, Aphelios kills the enemies of his faith in brooding silence—speaking only through the certainty of his aim, and the firing of each gun. Though fueled by a poison that renders him mute, he is guided by his sister Alune. From her distant temple sanctuary, she pushes an arsenal of moonstone weapons into his hands. For as long as the moon shines overhead, Aphelios will never be alone.

abilities.name: The Hitman and the Seer
abilities.description: Aphelios wields 5 Lunari Weapons made by his sister Alune. He has access to two at a time: one main-hand and one off-hand. Each weapon has a unique Basic Attack and Ability. Attacks and abilities consume a weapon's ammo. When out of ammo, Aphelios discards the weapon and Alune summons the next of the 5.

abilities.name: Weapon Abilites
abilities.description: Aphelios has 5 different activated abilities, based on his main-hand weapon:Calibrum (Rifle): Long range shot that marks its target for a long-range follow-up attack.Severum (Scythe Pistol): Run fast while attacking nearby enemies with both weapons.Gravitum (Cannon): Root all enemies slowed by this weapon.Infernum (Flamethrower): Blast enemies in a cone and attack them with your off-hand weapon.Crescendum (Chakram): Deploy a sentry that shoots your off-hand weapon.

abilities.name: Phase
abilities.description: Aphelios swaps his main-hand gun with his off-hand gun, replacing his basic attack and activated ability.

abilities.name: Weapon Queue System
abilities.description: Aphelios has no third ability. This slot shows the next weapon Alune will give him. Weapon order begins fixed but may change over game time -- when a weapon is out of ammo it goes to the end of the order.

abilities.name: Moonlight Vigil
abilities.description: Fire a concentrated blast of moonlight that explodes on enemy champions. Applies the unique effect of Aphelios' main-hand gun.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Weapon Abilites is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Aphelios's adc pressure.
Use Phase as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Weapon Queue System or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Lethal Tempo is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Aphelios does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Weapon Abilites and Weapon Queue System only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Moonlight Vigil should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 550 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Aphelios can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Aphelios's passive, The Hitman and the Seer, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Aphelios cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Moonlight Vigil sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Aphelios wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Aphelios tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Aphelios should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Aphelios wants to fight from.
If 45 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Aphelios's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Aphelios can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Kraken Slayer -> Infinity Edge -> Lord Dominik's Regards is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Aphelios's teamfight rating is 51/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Aphelios should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Aphelios, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Aphelios's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Aphelios's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Ranger's Focus is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Ashe's adc pressure.
Use Volley as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Hawkshot or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Lethal Tempo is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Ashe does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Ranger's Focus and Hawkshot only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Enchanted Crystal Arrow should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 600 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Ashe can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Ashe's passive, Frost Shot, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Ashe cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Enchanted Crystal Arrow sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Ashe wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Ashe tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Ashe should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Ashe wants to fight from.
If 48 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Ashe's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Ashe can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Kraken Slayer -> Infinity Edge -> Lord Dominik's Regards is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Ashe's teamfight rating is 54/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Ashe should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Ashe, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Ashe needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Ashe's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Ashe's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.title: The Star Forger
champions.blurb: Aurelion Sol once graced the vast emptiness of the cosmos with celestial wonders of his own devising. Now, he is forced to wield his awesome power at the behest of a space-faring empire that tricked him into servitude. Desiring a return to his...
champions.lore: Aurelion Sol once graced the vast emptiness of the cosmos with celestial wonders of his own devising. Now, he is forced to wield his awesome power at the behest of a space-faring empire that tricked him into servitude. Desiring a return to his star-forging ways, Aurelion Sol will drag the very stars from the sky, if he must, in order to regain his freedom.

abilities.name: Cosmic Creator
abilities.description: Aurelion Sol's damaging Abilities break down enemies into stacks of Stardust, which permanently improves each of his abilities.

abilities.name: Breath of Light
abilities.description: Aurelion Sol channels his dragon breath for a few seconds, damaging the first enemy hit and splashing reduced damage onto nearby enemies. Each second the breath is channeled directly at an enemy will deal bonus damage, which is improved by the amount of Stardust that's been collected. This ability collects Stardust if the target is a champion.

abilities.name: Astral Flight
abilities.description: Aurelion Sol flies over terrain in a targeted direction. While in this state, he can cast other abilities. Breath of Light no longer has a cooldown or maximum channel duration and deals increased damage while flying.Astral Flight's remaining cooldown is reduced whenever an enemy champion dies after being recently damaged by Aurelion Sol.Stardust increases Astral Flight's maximum range.

abilities.name: Singularity
abilities.description: Aurelion Sol summons a black hole, damaging enemies and slowly pulling them toward its center. This ability grants Stardust each time an enemy dies within the black hole and for each second an enemy champion is caught inside it. The center of the black hole executes enemies who are below a certain percentage of their maximum health. Stardust increases Singularity's area as well as the execution threshold.

abilities.name: Falling Star / The Skies Descend
abilities.description: Falling Star: Aurelion Sol crashes a star into the earth. This impact deals magic damage and stuns enemies while also granting Stardust for each enemy champion it hits. Gathering enough Stardust transforms Aurelion Sol's next Falling Star into The Skies Descend.The Skies Descend: Aurelion Sol drags a giant star down from the heavens with an increased impact zone and increased damage, knocking up enemies rather than stunning them. A shockwave then spreads from the edge of the impact zone, which damages and slows the enemies it hits. Stardust increases the impact area of both Falling Star and The Skies Descend.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Breath of Light is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Aurelion Sol's mid pressure.
Use Astral Flight as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Singularity or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Arcane Comet is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Aurelion Sol does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Breath of Light and Singularity only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Falling Star / The Skies Descend should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 550 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Aurelion Sol can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Aurelion Sol's passive, Cosmic Creator, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Aurelion Sol cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Falling Star / The Skies Descend sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Aurelion Sol wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Aurelion Sol tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Aurelion Sol should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Aurelion Sol wants to fight from.
If 48 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Aurelion Sol's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Aurelion Sol can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Stormsurge -> Rabadon's Deathcap is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Aurelion Sol's teamfight rating is 50/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Aurelion Sol should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Aurelion Sol, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Aurelion Sol needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Aurelion Sol's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Aurelion Sol's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.blurb: From the moment she was born, Aurora navigated life with a unique ability to move between the spirit and material realms. Determined to learn more about the spirit realm's inhabitants, she left her home to further her research and happened upon a...
champions.lore: From the moment she was born, Aurora navigated life with a unique ability to move between the spirit and material realms. Determined to learn more about the spirit realm's inhabitants, she left her home to further her research and happened upon a wayward demigod who'd become twisted and lost to time. Witnessing his desperation, Aurora resolved to find a way to help her feral friend regain his forgotten identity—a journey that would take her to the farthest reaches of the Freljord.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Twofold Hex is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Aurora's mid pressure.
Use Across the Veil as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with The Weirding or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Arcane Comet is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Aurora does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Twofold Hex and The Weirding only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Between Worlds should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 550 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Aurora can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Aurora's passive, Spirit Abjuration, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Aurora cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Between Worlds sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Aurora wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Aurora tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Aurora should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Aurora wants to fight from.
If 51 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Aurora's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Aurora can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Stormsurge -> Rabadon's Deathcap is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Aurora's teamfight rating is 45/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Aurora should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Aurora, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Aurora needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Aurora's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Aurora's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.lore: Azir was a mortal emperor of Shurima in a far distant age, a proud man who stood at the cusp of immortality. His hubris saw him betrayed and murdered at the moment of his greatest triumph, but now, millennia later, he has been reborn as an Ascended being of immense power. With his buried city risen from the sand, Azir seeks to restore Shurima to its former glory.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Conquering Sands is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Azir's mid pressure.
Use Arise! as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Shifting Sands or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Arcane Comet is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Azir does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Conquering Sands and Shifting Sands only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Emperor's Divide should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 525 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Azir can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Azir's passive, Shurima's Legacy, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Azir cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Emperor's Divide sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Azir wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Azir tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Azir should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Azir wants to fight from.
If 45 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Azir's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Azir can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Stormsurge -> Rabadon's Deathcap is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Azir's teamfight rating is 47/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Azir should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Azir, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Azir needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Azir's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Azir's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.title: the Wandering Caretaker
champions.blurb: A traveler from beyond the stars, Bard is an agent of serendipity who fights to maintain a balance where life can endure the indifference of chaos. Many Runeterrans sing songs that ponder his extraordinary nature, yet they all agree that the cosmic...
champions.lore: A traveler from beyond the stars, Bard is an agent of serendipity who fights to maintain a balance where life can endure the indifference of chaos. Many Runeterrans sing songs that ponder his extraordinary nature, yet they all agree that the cosmic vagabond is drawn to artifacts of great magical power. Surrounded by a jubilant choir of helpful spirit meeps, it is impossible to mistake his actions as malevolent, as Bard always serves the greater good... in his own odd way.

abilities.name: Traveler's Call
abilities.description: Meeps: Bard attracts lesser spirits that assist with his basic attacks to deal extra magic damage. When Bard has collected enough Chimes, his meeps will also deal damage in an area and slow enemies hit.Chimes: Ancient chimes randomly appear for Bard to collect. These grant experience, restore mana, and provide out of combat Move Speed.

abilities.name: Cosmic Binding
abilities.description: Bard fires a missile which will slow the first enemy struck, and continue onward. If it strikes a wall, it will stun the initial target; if it strikes another enemy, it will stun them both.

abilities.name: Caretaker's Shrine
abilities.description: Reveals a Health shrine which powers up over a short time, disappearing after healing and speeding up the first ally that touches it.

abilities.name: Magical Journey
abilities.description: Bard opens a portal in nearby terrain. Allies and enemies alike can take a one-way trip through that terrain by moving into the portal.

abilities.name: Tempered Fate
abilities.description: Bard sends spirit energy arcing to a location, putting all champions, minions, monsters, and turrets hit into stasis for a brief time.
