micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Cosmic Binding is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Bard's support pressure.
Use Caretaker's Shrine as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Magical Journey or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Summon Aery is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Bard does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Cosmic Binding and Magical Journey only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Tempered Fate should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 500 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Bard can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Bard's passive, Traveler's Call, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Bard cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Tempered Fate sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Bard wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Bard tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Bard should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Bard wants to fight from.
If 46 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Bard's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Bard can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Dream Maker -> Redemption -> Locket of the Iron Solari is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Bard's teamfight rating is 63/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Bard should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Bard, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Bard needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from grouped fights, controlled objective zones, and cooldown layering.
Monitor Bard's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Bard's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.name: Bel'Veth
champions.title: the Empress of the Void
champions.blurb: A nightmarish empress created from the raw material of an entire devoured city, Bel'Veth is the end of Runeterra itself... and the beginning of a monstrous reality of her own design. Driven by epochs of repurposed history, knowledge, and memories from...
champions.lore: A nightmarish empress created from the raw material of an entire devoured city, Bel'Veth is the end of Runeterra itself... and the beginning of a monstrous reality of her own design. Driven by epochs of repurposed history, knowledge, and memories from the world above, she voraciously feeds an ever-expanding need for new experiences and emotions, consuming all that crosses her path. Yet her wants could never be sated by only one world as she turns her hungry eyes toward the Void's old masters...

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Void Surge is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Bel'Veth's jungle pressure.
Use Above and Below as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Royal Maelstrom or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Conqueror is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Bel'Veth does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Void Surge and Royal Maelstrom only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Endless Banquet should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 150 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Bel'Veth can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Bel'Veth's passive, Death in Lavender , should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Bel'Veth cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Endless Banquet sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Bel'Veth wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Bel'Veth tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Bel'Veth should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Bel'Veth wants to fight from.
If 54 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Bel'Veth's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Bel'Veth can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Trinity Force -> Spear of Shojin -> Sterak's Gage is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Bel'Veth's teamfight rating is 46/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Bel'Veth should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Bel'Veth, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Bel'Veth needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Bel'Veth's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Bel'Veth's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.blurb: Blitzcrank is an enormous, near-indestructible automaton from Zaun, originally built to dispose of hazardous waste. However, he found this primary purpose too restricting, and modified his own form to better serve the fragile people of the Sump...
champions.lore: Blitzcrank is an enormous, near-indestructible automaton from Zaun, originally built to dispose of hazardous waste. However, he found this primary purpose too restricting, and modified his own form to better serve the fragile people of the Sump. Blitzcrank selflessly uses his strength and durability to protect others, extending a helpful metal fist or burst of energy to subdue any troublemakers.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Rocket Grab is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Blitzcrank's support pressure.
Use Overdrive as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Power Fist or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Aftershock is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Blitzcrank does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Rocket Grab and Power Fist only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Static Field should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 125 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Blitzcrank can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Blitzcrank's passive, Mana Barrier, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Blitzcrank cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Static Field sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Blitzcrank wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Blitzcrank tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Blitzcrank should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Blitzcrank wants to fight from.
If 42 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Blitzcrank's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Blitzcrank can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.

If Celestial Opposition -> Locket of the Iron Solari -> Knight's Vow is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Blitzcrank's teamfight rating is 63/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Blitzcrank should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Blitzcrank, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Blitzcrank needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from grouped fights, controlled objective zones, and cooldown layering.
Monitor Blitzcrank's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Blitzcrank's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.title: the Burning Vengeance
champions.blurb: Once a tribesman of the icy Freljord named Kegan Rodhe, the creature known as Brand is a lesson in the temptation of greater power. Seeking one of the legendary World Runes, Kegan betrayed his companions and seized it for himself—and, in an instant, the...
champions.lore: Once a tribesman of the icy Freljord named Kegan Rodhe, the creature known as Brand is a lesson in the temptation of greater power. Seeking one of the legendary World Runes, Kegan betrayed his companions and seized it for himself—and, in an instant, the man was no more. His soul burned away, his body a vessel of living flame, Brand now roams Valoran in search of other Runes, swearing revenge for wrongs he could never possibly have suffered in a dozen mortal lifetimes.

abilities.name: Blaze
abilities.description: Brand's spells light his targets ablaze, dealing damage over 4 seconds, stacking up to 3 times. If Brand kills an enemy while it is ablaze he regains mana. When Blaze reaches max stacks on a Champion or large monster, it becomes unstable. It detonates in 2 seconds, applying spell effects and dealing massive damage in an area around the victim.

abilities.name: Sear
abilities.description: Brand launches a ball of fire forward that deals magic damage. If the target is ablaze, Sear will stun the target.

abilities.name: Pillar of Flame
abilities.description: After a short delay, Brand creates a Pillar of Flame at a target area, dealing magic damage to enemy units within the area. Units that are ablaze take an additional 25% damage.

abilities.name: Conflagration
abilities.description: Brand conjures a powerful blast at his target that spreads to nearby enemies, dealing magic damage. If the target is ablaze, Conflagration's spread is doubled.

abilities.name: Pyroclasm
abilities.description: Brand unleashes a devastating torrent of fire that bounces up to 5 times off of Brand and nearby enemies, dealing magic damage to enemies each time bounce. Bounces prioritize stacking Blaze to max on Champions. If a target is ablaze, Pyroclasm will briefly slow them.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Sear is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Brand's jungle pressure.
Use Pillar of Flame as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Conflagration or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Conqueror is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Brand does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Sear and Conflagration only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Pyroclasm should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 550 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Brand can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Brand's passive, Blaze, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Brand cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Pyroclasm sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Brand wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Brand tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Brand should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Brand wants to fight from.
If 58 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Brand's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Brand can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Stormsurge -> Rabadon's Deathcap is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Brand's teamfight rating is 50/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Brand should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Brand, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Brand needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Brand's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Brand's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.title: the Heart of the Freljord
champions.blurb: Blessed with massive biceps and an even bigger heart, Braum is a beloved hero of the Freljord. Every mead hall north of Frostheld toasts his legendary strength, said to have felled a forest of oaks in a single night, and punched an entire mountain into...
champions.lore: Blessed with massive biceps and an even bigger heart, Braum is a beloved hero of the Freljord. Every mead hall north of Frostheld toasts his legendary strength, said to have felled a forest of oaks in a single night, and punched an entire mountain into rubble. Bearing an enchanted vault door as his shield, Braum roams the frozen north sporting a mustachioed smile as big as his muscles—a true friend to all those in need.

abilities.name: Concussive Blows
abilities.description: Braum's basic attacks apply Concussive Blows. Once the first stack is applied, ally basic attacks also stack Concussive Blows. Upon reaching 4 stacks, the target is stunned and takes magic damage. For the next few seconds they cannot receive new stacks, but take bonus magic damage from Braum's attacks.

abilities.name: Winter's Bite
abilities.description: Braum propels freezing ice from his shield, slowing and dealing magic damage.Applies a stack of Concussive Blows.

abilities.name: Stand Behind Me
abilities.description: Braum leaps to a target allied champion or minion. On arrival, Braum and the ally gain Armor and Magic Resist for a few seconds.

abilities.name: Unbreakable
abilities.description: Braum raises his shield in a direction for several seconds, intercepting all projectiles causing them to hit him and be destroyed. He negates the damage of the first attack completely and reduces the damage of all subsequent attacks from this direction.

abilities.name: Glacial Fissure
abilities.description: Braum slams the ground, knocking up enemies nearby and in a line in front of him. A fissure is left along the line that slows enemies.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Winter's Bite is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Braum's support pressure.
Use Stand Behind Me as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Unbreakable or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Aftershock is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Braum does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Winter's Bite and Unbreakable only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Glacial Fissure should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 125 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Braum can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Braum's passive, Concussive Blows, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Braum cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Glacial Fissure sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Braum wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Braum tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Braum should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Braum wants to fight from.
If 44 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Braum's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Braum can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.

If Celestial Opposition -> Locket of the Iron Solari -> Knight's Vow is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Braum's teamfight rating is 65/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Braum should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Braum, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Braum needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from grouped fights, controlled objective zones, and cooldown layering.
Monitor Braum's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Braum's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.name: Briar
champions.title: the Restrained Hunger
champions.blurb: A failed experiment by the Black Rose, Briar's uncontrollable bloodlust required a special pillory to focus her frenzied mind. After years of confinement, this living weapon broke free from her restraints and unleashed herself into the world. Now she's...
champions.lore: A failed experiment by the Black Rose, Briar's uncontrollable bloodlust required a special pillory to focus her frenzied mind. After years of confinement, this living weapon broke free from her restraints and unleashed herself into the world. Now she's controlled by no one—following only her hunger for knowledge and blood—and relishes the opportunities to let loose, even if reining back the frenzy isn't easy.

abilities.name: Crimson Curse
abilities.description: Briar's attacks and abilities apply a stacking bleed that heals her for a portion of the damage it deals. Perpetually hungry, she gains increased healing based on her missing Health, but lacks innate Health Regeneration.

abilities.name: Head Rush
abilities.description: Briar leaps to a unit and hits enemies with The Heel Wheel (of Pain), stunning them and breaking their Armor.

abilities.name: Blood Frenzy / Snack Attack
abilities.description: Briar leaps forward and shatters her pillory, entering a Blood Frenzy that causes her to relentlessly pursue the nearest enemy (prioritizing champions). While frenzied, she gains increased Attack Speed and Move Speed, and her attacks deal damage in an area around her target.Briar can reactivate this ability while frenzied to take a CHOMP out of her target on her next attack, dealing additional damage based on their missing Health, and healing Briar based on the damage she deals.

abilities.name: Chilling Scream
abilities.description: Briar refocuses her mind, removing Blood Frenzy and channeling energy into a powerful scream that damages and slows enemies. While charging, she takes reduced damage and heals for a portion of her max Health. A fully charged scream knocks foes back, dealing additional damage and stunning those who collide with a wall.

abilities.name: Certain Death
abilities.description: Briar kicks her pillory's hemolith gemstone, marking the first champion it hits as her prey. She then beelines straight to them, fearing other surrounding enemies upon arriving at her target, and enters a state of complete hemomania. She will pursue her prey until death, gaining the benefits of Blood Frenzy as well as additional Armor, Magic Resistance, Life Steal, and Move Speed.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Head Rush is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Briar's jungle pressure.
Use Blood Frenzy / Snack Attack as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Chilling Scream or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Conqueror is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Briar does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Head Rush and Chilling Scream only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Certain Death should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 125 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Briar can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Briar's passive, Crimson Curse, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Briar cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Certain Death sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Briar wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Briar tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Briar should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Briar wants to fight from.
If 56 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Briar's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Briar can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Trinity Force -> Spear of Shojin -> Sterak's Gage is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Briar's teamfight rating is 52/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Briar should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Briar, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Briar needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Briar's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Briar's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.lore: Renowned as its finest peacekeeper, Caitlyn Kiramman is also Piltover's best shot at ridding the city of its elusive criminal elements. She is often paired with Vi, acting as a cool counterpoint to her partner's more impetuous nature. Even though she carries a one-of-a-kind hextech rifle, Caitlyn's most powerful weapon is her superior intellect, allowing her to lay elaborate traps for any lawbreakers foolish enough to operate in the City of Progress.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Piltover Peacemaker is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Caitlyn's adc pressure.
Use Yordle Snap Trap as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with 90 Caliber Net or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Lethal Tempo is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Caitlyn does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Piltover Peacemaker and 90 Caliber Net only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Ace in the Hole should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 650 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Caitlyn can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Caitlyn's passive, Headshot, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Caitlyn cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Ace in the Hole sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Caitlyn wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Caitlyn tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Caitlyn should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Caitlyn wants to fight from.
If 50 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Caitlyn's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Caitlyn can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Kraken Slayer -> Infinity Edge -> Lord Dominik's Regards is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Caitlyn's teamfight rating is 46/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Caitlyn should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Caitlyn, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Caitlyn needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Caitlyn's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Caitlyn's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.title: the Steel Shadow
champions.blurb: Weaponized to operate outside the boundaries of the law, Camille is the Principal Intelligencer of Clan Ferros—an elegant and elite agent who ensures the Piltover machine and its Zaunite underbelly runs smoothly. Adaptable and precise, she views sloppy...
champions.lore: Weaponized to operate outside the boundaries of the law, Camille is the Principal Intelligencer of Clan Ferros—an elegant and elite agent who ensures the Piltover machine and its Zaunite underbelly runs smoothly. Adaptable and precise, she views sloppy technique as an embarrassment that must be put to order. With a mind as sharp as the blades she bears, Camille's pursuit of superiority through hextech body augmentation has left many to wonder if she is now more machine than woman.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Precision Protocol is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Camille's top pressure.
Use Tactical Sweep as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Hookshot or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Conqueror is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Camille does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Precision Protocol and Hookshot only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
The Hextech Ultimatum should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 125 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Camille can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Camille's passive, Adaptive Defenses, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Camille cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and The Hextech Ultimatum sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Camille wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Camille tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Camille should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Camille wants to fight from.
If 46 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Camille's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Camille can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Trinity Force -> Spear of Shojin -> Sterak's Gage is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Camille's teamfight rating is 52/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Camille should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Camille, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Camille needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Camille's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Camille's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.title: the Serpent's Embrace
champions.blurb: Cassiopeia is a deadly creature bent on manipulating others to her sinister will. Youngest and most beautiful daughter of the noble Du Couteau family of Noxus, she ventured deep into the crypts beneath Shurima in search of ancient power. There, she was...
champions.lore: Cassiopeia is a deadly creature bent on manipulating others to her sinister will. Youngest and most beautiful daughter of the noble Du Couteau family of Noxus, she ventured deep into the crypts beneath Shurima in search of ancient power. There, she was bitten by a gruesome tomb guardian, whose venom transformed her into a viper-like predator. Cunning and agile, Cassiopeia now slithers under the veil of night, petrifying her enemies with her baleful gaze.
