competitive.patchTrend: Master Yi needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
competitive.metaEvolution: Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Alpha Strike is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Master Yi's jungle pressure.
Use Meditate as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Wuju Style or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Conqueror is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Master Yi does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Alpha Strike and Wuju Style only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Highlander should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 175 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Master Yi can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Master Yi's passive, Double Strike, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Master Yi cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Highlander sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Master Yi wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Master Yi tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Master Yi should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Master Yi wants to fight from.
If 54 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Master Yi's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Master Yi can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Trinity Force -> Spear of Shojin -> Sterak's Gage is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Master Yi's teamfight rating is 45/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Master Yi should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Master Yi, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Master Yi needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Master Yi's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Master Yi's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.title: the Soul's Reflection
champions.blurb: Mel Medarda is the presumed heir of the Medarda family, once one of the most powerful in Noxus. In appearance she is a graceful aristocrat, but beneath the surface lies a skilled politician who makes it her business to know everything about everyone she...
champions.lore: Mel Medarda is the presumed heir of the Medarda family, once one of the most powerful in Noxus. In appearance she is a graceful aristocrat, but beneath the surface lies a skilled politician who makes it her business to know everything about everyone she meets. After an encounter with the mysterious Black Rose, Mel discovered the depths of her mother's deception and, for once, faced a situation potentially beyond her control. With newly awakened magical abilities, she sailed home in search of answers—and though many still seek to temper the light within her, Mel's soul remains forever defiant.

abilities.name: Searing Brilliance
abilities.description: Whenever Mel uses an ability, she gains three bonus projectiles (up to nine maximum) on her next attack.When Mel deals damage through an ability or attack, she applies Overwhelm, which can stack infinitely. If the enemy is hit by Mel with enough Overwhelm damage, the stacks are consumed to execute the target.

abilities.name: Radiant Volley

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Radiant Volley is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Mel's mid pressure.
Use Rebuttal as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Solar Snare or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Arcane Comet is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Mel does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Radiant Volley and Solar Snare only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Golden Eclipse should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 550 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Mel can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Mel's passive, Searing Brilliance, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Mel cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Golden Eclipse sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Mel wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Mel tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Mel should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Mel wants to fight from.
If 46 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Mel's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Mel can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Stormsurge -> Rabadon's Deathcap is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Mel's teamfight rating is 50/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Mel should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Mel, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Mel needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Mel's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Mel's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.lore: Milio is a warmhearted boy from Ixtal who has, despite his young age, mastered the fire axiom and discovered something new: soothing fire. With this newfound power, Milio plans to help his family escape their exile by joining the Yun Tal—just like his grandmother once did. Having traveled through the Ixtal jungles to the capital of Ixaocan, Milio now prepares to face the Vidalion and join the Yun Tal, unaware of the trials—and dangers—that await him.

abilities.description: Milio's abilities enchant allies on touch, making their next damage deal a burst of extra damage and burn the target.

abilities.description: Kick a ball that knocks back an enemy. The ball launches upward on hit and falls toward the enemy, damaging and slowing enemies in the area upon impact.

abilities.name: Breath of Life

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Ultra Mega Fire Kick is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Milio's support pressure.
Use Cozy Campfire as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Warm Hugs or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Summon Aery is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Milio does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Ultra Mega Fire Kick and Warm Hugs only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Breath of Life should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 525 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Milio can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Milio's passive, Fired Up!, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Milio cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Breath of Life sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Milio wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Milio tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Milio should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Milio wants to fight from.
If 45 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Milio's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Milio can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Dream Maker -> Redemption -> Locket of the Iron Solari is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Milio's teamfight rating is 61/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Milio should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Milio, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Milio needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from grouped fights, controlled objective zones, and cooldown layering.
Monitor Milio's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Milio's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.lore: A Bilgewater captain famed for her looks but feared for her ruthlessness, Sarah Fortune paints a stark figure among the hardened criminals of the port city. As a child, she witnessed the reaver king Gangplank murder her family—an act she brutally avenged years later, blowing up his flagship while he was still aboard. Those who underestimate her will face a beguiling and unpredictable opponent… and, likely, a bullet or two in their guts.

competitive.metaEvolution: Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Double Up is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Miss Fortune's adc pressure.
Use Strut as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Make It Rain or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Lethal Tempo is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Miss Fortune does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Double Up and Make It Rain only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Bullet Time should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 550 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Miss Fortune can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Miss Fortune's passive, Love Tap, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Miss Fortune cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Bullet Time sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Miss Fortune wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Miss Fortune tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Miss Fortune should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Miss Fortune wants to fight from.
If 44 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Miss Fortune's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Miss Fortune can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Kraken Slayer -> Infinity Edge -> Lord Dominik's Regards is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Miss Fortune's teamfight rating is 43/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Miss Fortune should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Miss Fortune, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Miss Fortune's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Obliterate is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Mordekaiser's top pressure.
Use Indestructible as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Death's Grasp or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Conqueror is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Mordekaiser does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Obliterate and Death's Grasp only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Realm of Death should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 175 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Mordekaiser can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Mordekaiser's passive, Darkness Rise, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Mordekaiser cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Realm of Death sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Mordekaiser wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Mordekaiser tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Mordekaiser should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Mordekaiser wants to fight from.
If 49 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Mordekaiser's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Mordekaiser can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Trinity Force -> Spear of Shojin -> Sterak's Gage is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Mordekaiser's teamfight rating is 54/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Mordekaiser should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Mordekaiser, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Mordekaiser needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Mordekaiser's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Mordekaiser's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.lore: Conflicted between her celestial and mortal natures, Morgana bound her wings to embrace humanity, and inflicts her pain and bitterness upon the dishonest and the corrupt. She rejects laws and traditions she believes are unjust, and fights for truth from the shadows of Demacia—even as others seek to repress it—by casting shields and chains of dark fire. More than anything else, Morgana truly believes that even the banished and outcast may one day rise again.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Dark Binding is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Morgana's support pressure.
Use Tormented Shadow as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Black Shield or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Summon Aery is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Morgana does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Dark Binding and Black Shield only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Soul Shackles should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 450 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Morgana can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Morgana's passive, Soul Siphon, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Morgana cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Soul Shackles sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Morgana wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Morgana tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Morgana should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Morgana wants to fight from.
If 51 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Morgana's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Morgana can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Dream Maker -> Redemption -> Locket of the Iron Solari is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Morgana's teamfight rating is 59/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Morgana should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Morgana, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Morgana needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Morgana's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Morgana's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.lore: Across the sands of Shurima, a chorus of howls rings out. It is the call of the dune hounds, voracious predators who form packs and compete for the right to hunt in these barren lands. Among them, one pack stands above all, for they are driven not only by canine instincts, but by the ancient power of the Darkin.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Darkin Daggers is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Naafiri's mid pressure.
Use The Call of the Pack as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Eviscerate or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Electrocute is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Naafiri does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Darkin Daggers and Eviscerate only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Hounds' Pursuit should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 125 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Naafiri can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Naafiri's passive, We Are More, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Naafiri cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Hounds' Pursuit sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Naafiri wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Naafiri tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Naafiri should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Naafiri wants to fight from.
If 42 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Naafiri's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Naafiri can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Youmuu's Ghostblade -> Opportunity -> Edge of Night is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Naafiri's teamfight rating is 43/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Naafiri should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Naafiri, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Naafiri needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Naafiri's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Naafiri's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.lore: A headstrong young vastaya of the seas, Nami was the first of the Marai tribe to leave the waves and venture onto dry land, when their ancient accord with the Targonians was broken. With no other option, she took it upon herself to complete the sacred ritual that would ensure the safety of her people. Amidst the chaos of this new age, Nami faces an uncertain future with grit and determination, using her Tidecaller staff to summon the strength of the oceans themselves.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Aqua Prison is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Nami's support pressure.
Use Ebb and Flow as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Tidecaller's Blessing or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Summon Aery is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Nami does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Aqua Prison and Tidecaller's Blessing only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Tidal Wave should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 550 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Nami can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Nami's passive, Surging Tides, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Nami cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Tidal Wave sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Nami wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Nami tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Nami should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Nami wants to fight from.
If 49 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Nami's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Nami can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Dream Maker -> Redemption -> Locket of the Iron Solari is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Nami's teamfight rating is 61/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Nami should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Nami, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Nami needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Nami's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Nami's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.title: the Curator of the Sands
champions.blurb: Nasus is an imposing, jackal-headed Ascended being from ancient Shurima, a heroic figure regarded as a demigod by the people of the desert. Fiercely intelligent, he was a guardian of knowledge and peerless strategist whose wisdom guided the ancient...
champions.lore: Nasus is an imposing, jackal-headed Ascended being from ancient Shurima, a heroic figure regarded as a demigod by the people of the desert. Fiercely intelligent, he was a guardian of knowledge and peerless strategist whose wisdom guided the ancient empire of Shurima to greatness for many centuries. After the fall of the empire, he went into self-imposed exile, becoming little more than a legend. Now that the ancient city of Shurima has risen once more, he has returned, determined to ensure it never falls again.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Siphoning Strike is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Nasus's top pressure.
Use Wither as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Spirit Fire or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Conqueror is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Nasus does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Siphoning Strike and Spirit Fire only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Fury of the Sands should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 125 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Nasus can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Nasus's passive, Soul Eater, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Nasus cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Fury of the Sands sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Nasus wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Nasus tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Nasus should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Nasus wants to fight from.
If 48 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Nasus's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Nasus can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Trinity Force -> Spear of Shojin -> Sterak's Gage is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Nasus's teamfight rating is 53/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Nasus should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Nasus, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Nasus needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Nasus's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Nasus's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.title: the Titan of the Depths
champions.blurb: A lonely legend as old as the first piers sunk in Bilgewater, the armored goliath known as Nautilus roams the dark waters off the coast of the Blue Flame Isles. Driven by a forgotten betrayal, he strikes without warning, swinging his enormous anchor to...
champions.lore: A lonely legend as old as the first piers sunk in Bilgewater, the armored goliath known as Nautilus roams the dark waters off the coast of the Blue Flame Isles. Driven by a forgotten betrayal, he strikes without warning, swinging his enormous anchor to save the wretched, and drag the greedy to their doom. It is said he comes for those who forget to pay the “Bilgewater tithe”, pulling them down beneath the waves with him—an iron-clad reminder that none can escape the depths.

abilities.description: Nautilus gains a temporary Shield. While it persists, his Attacks deal damage over time to his target and surrounding enemies.

abilities.name: Riptide
abilities.description: Nautilus creates three exploding waves around himself. Each explosion damages and slows enemies.

abilities.name: Depth Charge
abilities.description: Nautilus fires a shockwave into the earth that chases an opponent. This shockwave rips up the earth above it, knocking enemies into the air. When it reaches the opponent, the shockwave erupts, knocking his target into the air and stunning them.
