micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Vault Breaker is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Vi's jungle pressure.
Use Denting Blows as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Relentless Force or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Conqueror is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Vi does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Vault Breaker and Relentless Force only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Cease and Desist should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 125 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Vi can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Vi's passive, Blast Shield, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Vi cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Cease and Desist sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Vi wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Vi tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Vi should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Vi wants to fight from.
If 58 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Vi's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Vi can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Trinity Force -> Spear of Shojin -> Sterak's Gage is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Vi's teamfight rating is 54/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Vi should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Vi, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Vi needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Vi's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Vi's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.lore: Once ruler of a long-lost kingdom, Viego perished over a thousand years ago when his attempt to bring his wife back from the dead triggered the magical catastrophe known as the Ruination. Transformed into a powerful, unliving specter tortured by an obsessive longing for his centuries-dead queen, Viego now stands as the Ruined King, controlling the deadly Harrowings as he scours Runeterra for anything that might one day restore her, and destroying all in his path as the Black Mist pours endlessly from his cruel, broken heart.

abilities.description: Enemies who fall before Viego become wraiths. By attacking a wraith, Viego temporarily seizes control of the dead enemy's body, healing for a percentage of his target's max health and gaining access to their basic abilities and items. He replaces their Ultimate with a free cast of his own.

competitive.metaEvolution: Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Blade of the Ruined King is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Viego's jungle pressure.
Use Spectral Maw as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Harrowed Path or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Conqueror is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Viego does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Blade of the Ruined King and Harrowed Path only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Heartbreaker should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 200 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Viego can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Viego's passive, Sovereign's Domination, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Viego cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Heartbreaker sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Viego wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Viego tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Viego should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Viego wants to fight from.
If 55 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Viego's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Viego can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Trinity Force -> Spear of Shojin -> Sterak's Gage is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Viego's teamfight rating is 45/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Viego should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Viego, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Viego needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Viego's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Viego's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.name: Viktor
champions.title: the Herald of the Arcane
champions.blurb: The fully biomechanical evolution of his former self, Viktor has embraced his Glorious Evolution and become something of a messiah to his followers. He sacrificed his own humanity under the logic that eliminating emotion would thereby eliminate...
champions.lore: The fully biomechanical evolution of his former self, Viktor has embraced his Glorious Evolution and become something of a messiah to his followers. He sacrificed his own humanity under the logic that eliminating emotion would thereby eliminate suffering—and now seeks to bring the revelation of the hexcore to the rest of the world, even if they're incapable of understanding the benefit. After all, to this master of the arcane, violence is merely a variable necessary to balance the ultimate equation.

abilities.name: Glorious Evolution
abilities.description: Viktor gains Hex Fragments whenever he kills an enemy. With every 100 Hex Fragments he obtains, Viktor permanently augments an active ability. After upgrading all of his basic abilities, he can gather 100 Hex Fragments to augment his ultimate ability.

abilities.description: Viktor blasts an enemy unit with magic damage, which grants him a shield and empowers his next basic attack.Augment: Siphon Power's shield is increased by 60% and Viktor gains bonus move speed after casting the Ability.

abilities.name: Gravity Field
abilities.description: Viktor conjures a heavy gravitational field that slows enemies caught within its radius. Enemies who stay in the field for too long become stunned.Augment: Viktor's spells apply a slow to enemies.

abilities.name: Hextech Ray
abilities.description: Viktor uses his biomechanical arm to fire a Hextech Ray that cuts across the field in a line, dealing damage to all enemies in its path.Augment: An explosion follows in the Hextech Ray's wake, dealing magic damage.

abilities.name: Arcane Storm
abilities.description: Viktor conjures an Arcane Storm on the field, dealing magic damage and interrupting enemy channels. The storm periodically does magic damage to all nearby enemies and can be redirected by Viktor.Augment: The Arcane Storm moves 25% faster, and whenever champions die after taking damage from it, the storm grows and increases in its duration.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Siphon Power is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Viktor's mid pressure.
Use Gravity Field as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Hextech Ray or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Arcane Comet is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Viktor does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Siphon Power and Hextech Ray only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Arcane Storm should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 525 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Viktor can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Viktor's passive, Glorious Evolution, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Viktor cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Arcane Storm sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Viktor wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Viktor tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Viktor should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Viktor wants to fight from.
If 43 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Viktor's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Viktor can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Stormsurge -> Rabadon's Deathcap is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Viktor's teamfight rating is 51/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Viktor should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Viktor, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Viktor needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Viktor's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Viktor's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.title: the Crimson Reaper
champions.blurb: A fiend with a thirst for mortal blood, Vladimir has influenced the affairs of Noxus since the empire's earliest days. In addition to unnaturally extending his life, his mastery of hemomancy allows him to control the minds and bodies of others as easily...
champions.lore: A fiend with a thirst for mortal blood, Vladimir has influenced the affairs of Noxus since the empire's earliest days. In addition to unnaturally extending his life, his mastery of hemomancy allows him to control the minds and bodies of others as easily as his own. In the flamboyant salons of the Noxian aristocracy, this has enabled him to build a fanatical cult of personality around himself—while in the lowest back alleys, it allows him to bleed his enemies dry.

abilities.name: Crimson Pact
abilities.description: Every 30 points of bonus Health gives Vladimir 1 Ability Power and every 1 point of Ability Power gives Vladimir 1.6 bonus Health (does not stack with itself).

abilities.name: Transfusion
abilities.description: Vladimir steals life from the target enemy. When Vladimir's resource is full, Transfusion will benefit from massively increased damage and healing for a brief time.

abilities.name: Sanguine Pool
abilities.description: Vladimir sinks into a pool of blood, becoming untargetable for 2 seconds. Additionally, enemies on the pool are slowed and Vladimir siphons life from them.

abilities.name: Tides of Blood
abilities.description: Vladimir pays his own health to charge up a reservoir of blood which, when released, deals damage in the area around him but can be blocked by enemy units.

abilities.name: Hemoplague
abilities.description: Vladimir infects an area with a virulent plague. Affected enemies take increased damage for the duration. After a few seconds, Hemoplague deals magic damage to infected enemies and heals Vladimir for each enemy Champion hit.

competitive.metaEvolution: Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Transfusion is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Vladimir's mid pressure.
Use Sanguine Pool as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Tides of Blood or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Arcane Comet is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Vladimir does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Transfusion and Tides of Blood only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Hemoplague should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 450 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Vladimir can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Vladimir's passive, Crimson Pact, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Vladimir cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Hemoplague sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Vladimir wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Vladimir tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Vladimir should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Vladimir wants to fight from.
If 48 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Vladimir's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Vladimir can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Stormsurge -> Rabadon's Deathcap is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Vladimir's teamfight rating is 49/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Vladimir should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Vladimir, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Vladimir needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Vladimir's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Vladimir's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.title: the Relentless Storm
champions.blurb: To those who still revere him, the Volibear is the storm made manifest. Destructive, wild, and stubbornly resolute, he existed before mortals walked the Freljord's tundra, and is fiercely protective of the lands that he and his demi-god kin created...
champions.lore: To those who still revere him, the Volibear is the storm made manifest. Destructive, wild, and stubbornly resolute, he existed before mortals walked the Freljord's tundra, and is fiercely protective of the lands that he and his demi-god kin created. Cultivating a deep hatred of civilization and the weakness it brought with it, he now fights to return to the old ways—when the land was untamed, and blood spilled freely—and eagerly battles all who oppose him, with tooth, claw, and thundering domination.

competitive.metaEvolution: Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Thundering Smash is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Volibear's top pressure.
Use Frenzied Maul as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Sky Splitter or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Conqueror is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Volibear does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Thundering Smash and Sky Splitter only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Stormbringer should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 150 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Volibear can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Volibear's passive, The Relentless Storm, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Volibear cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Stormbringer sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Volibear wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Volibear tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Volibear should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Volibear wants to fight from.
If 48 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Volibear's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Volibear can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Trinity Force -> Spear of Shojin -> Sterak's Gage is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Volibear's teamfight rating is 49/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Volibear should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Volibear, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Volibear needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Volibear's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Volibear's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.title: the Uncaged Wrath of Zaun
champions.blurb: Warwick is a monster who hunts the gray alleys of Zaun. Transformed by agonizing experiments, his body is fused with an intricate system of chambers and pumps, machinery filling his veins with alchemical rage. He bursts from the shadows to prey upon...
champions.lore: Warwick is a monster who hunts the gray alleys of Zaun. Transformed by agonizing experiments, his body is fused with an intricate system of chambers and pumps, machinery filling his veins with alchemical rage. He bursts from the shadows to prey upon those criminals who terrorize the city's depths. Warwick is drawn to blood, driven mad by its scent… and none who spill it can escape him.

abilities.name: Eternal Hunger
abilities.description: Warwick's basic attacks deal bonus magic damage. If Warwick is below 50% health, he heals the same amount. If Warwick is below 25% health, this healing triples.

abilities.name: Jaws of the Beast
abilities.description: Warwick lunges forward and bites his target, dealing damage based on their maximum health and healing for damage dealt.

abilities.name: Blood Hunt
abilities.description: Warwick senses enemies below 50% health, gaining Move Speed toward and attack speed against them. When they fall below 25% health, he frenzies and these bonuses triple.

abilities.name: Primal Howl
abilities.description: Warwick gains damage reduction for 2.5 seconds. At the end, or if re-activated, he howls, causing nearby enemies to flee for 1 second.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Jaws of the Beast is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Warwick's jungle pressure.
Use Blood Hunt as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Primal Howl or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Conqueror is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Warwick does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Jaws of the Beast and Primal Howl only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Infinite Duress should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 125 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Warwick can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Warwick's passive, Eternal Hunger, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Warwick cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Infinite Duress sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Warwick wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Warwick tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Warwick should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Warwick wants to fight from.
If 52 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Warwick's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Warwick can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Trinity Force -> Spear of Shojin -> Sterak's Gage is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Warwick's teamfight rating is 47/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Warwick should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Warwick, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Warwick needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Warwick's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Warwick's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.blurb: Wukong is a vastayan trickster who uses his strength, agility, and intelligence to confuse his opponents and gain the upper hand. After finding a lifelong friend in the warrior known as Master Yi, Wukong became the last student of the ancient martial...
champions.lore: Wukong is a vastayan trickster who uses his strength, agility, and intelligence to confuse his opponents and gain the upper hand. After finding a lifelong friend in the warrior known as Master Yi, Wukong became the last student of the ancient martial art known as Wuju. Armed with an enchanted staff, Wukong seeks to prevent Ionia from falling to ruin.

abilities.description: Wukong gains stacking armor and max health regeneration while fighting champions and monsters.

abilities.name: Crushing Blow

abilities.name: Nimbus Strike

abilities.name: Cyclone

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Crushing Blow is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Wukong's jungle pressure.
Use Warrior Trickster as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Nimbus Strike or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Conqueror is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Wukong does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Crushing Blow and Nimbus Strike only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Cyclone should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 175 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Wukong can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Wukong's passive, Stone Skin, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Wukong cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Cyclone sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Wukong wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Wukong tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Wukong should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Wukong wants to fight from.
If 50 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Wukong's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Wukong can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Trinity Force -> Spear of Shojin -> Sterak's Gage is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Wukong's teamfight rating is 53/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Wukong should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Wukong, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Wukong needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Wukong's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Wukong's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Double Daggers is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Xayah's adc pressure.
Use Deadly Plumage as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Bladecaller or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Lethal Tempo is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Xayah does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Double Daggers and Bladecaller only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Featherstorm should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 525 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Xayah can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Xayah's passive, Clean Cuts, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Xayah cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Featherstorm sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Xayah wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Xayah tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Xayah should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Xayah wants to fight from.
If 52 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Xayah's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Xayah can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Kraken Slayer -> Infinity Edge -> Lord Dominik's Regards is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Xayah's teamfight rating is 55/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Xayah should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Xayah, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Xayah needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Xayah's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Xayah's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

For millennia, he was trapped beneath the desert sands, but the rise of Shurima freed him from his ancient prison. Driven insane with power, he now seeks to take what he believes is rightfully his and replace the upstart civilizations of the world with one fashioned in his image.
