competitive.metaEvolution: Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Razor Shuriken is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Zed's jungle pressure.
Use Living Shadow as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Shadow Slash or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Conqueror is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Zed does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Razor Shuriken and Shadow Slash only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Death Mark should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 125 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Zed can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Zed's passive, Contempt for the Weak, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Zed cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Death Mark sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Zed wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Zed tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Zed should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Zed wants to fight from.
If 52 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Zed's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Zed can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Youmuu's Ghostblade -> Opportunity -> Edge of Night is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Zed's teamfight rating is 43/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Zed should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Zed, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Zed needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Zed's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Zed's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.title: The Spark of Zaun
champions.blurb: A headstrong, spirited young woman from Zaun's working-class, Zeri channels her electric magic to charge herself and her custom-crafted gun. Her volatile power mirrors her emotions, its sparks reflecting her lightning-fast approach to life. Deeply...
champions.lore: A headstrong, spirited young woman from Zaun's working-class, Zeri channels her electric magic to charge herself and her custom-crafted gun. Her volatile power mirrors her emotions, its sparks reflecting her lightning-fast approach to life. Deeply compassionate toward others, Zeri carries the love of her family and her home into every fight. Though her eagerness to help can sometimes backfire, Zeri believes one truth to be certain: stand up for your community, and it will stand up with you.

competitive.metaEvolution: Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Burst Fire is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Zeri's adc pressure.
Use Ultrashock Laser as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Spark Surge or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Lethal Tempo is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Zeri does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Burst Fire and Spark Surge only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Lightning Crash should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 550 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Zeri can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Zeri's passive, Living Battery, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Zeri cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Lightning Crash sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Zeri wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Zeri tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Zeri should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Zeri wants to fight from.
If 44 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Zeri's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Zeri can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Kraken Slayer -> Infinity Edge -> Lord Dominik's Regards is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Zeri's teamfight rating is 45/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Zeri should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Zeri, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Zeri needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Zeri's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Zeri's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.lore: With a love of big bombs and short fuses, the yordle Ziggs is an explosive force of nature. As an inventor's assistant in Piltover, he was bored by his predictable life and befriended a mad, blue-haired bomber named Jinx. After a wild night on the town, Ziggs took her advice and moved to Zaun, where he now explores his fascinations more freely, terrorizing the chem-barons and regular citizens alike in his never ending quest to blow stuff up.

Ziggs is also knocked away, but takes no damage. Ziggs can use the Satchel to hexplode vulnerable enemy turrets.

competitive.metaEvolution: Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Bouncing Bomb is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Ziggs's adc pressure.
Use Satchel Charge as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Hexplosive Minefield or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Arcane Comet is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Ziggs does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Bouncing Bomb and Hexplosive Minefield only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Mega Inferno Bomb should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 550 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Ziggs can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Ziggs's passive, Short Fuse, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Ziggs cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Mega Inferno Bomb sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Ziggs wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Ziggs tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Ziggs should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Ziggs wants to fight from.
If 44 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Ziggs's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Ziggs can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Stormsurge -> Rabadon's Deathcap is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Ziggs's teamfight rating is 46/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Ziggs should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Ziggs, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Ziggs needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Ziggs's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Ziggs's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.name: Zilean
champions.title: the Chronokeeper
champions.blurb: Once a powerful Icathian mage, Zilean became obsessed with the passage of time after witnessing his homeland's destruction by the Void. Unable to spare even a minute to grieve the catastrophic loss, he called upon ancient temporal magic to divine all...
champions.lore: Once a powerful Icathian mage, Zilean became obsessed with the passage of time after witnessing his homeland's destruction by the Void. Unable to spare even a minute to grieve the catastrophic loss, he called upon ancient temporal magic to divine all possible outcomes. Having become functionally immortal, Zilean now drifts through the past, present, and future, bending and warping the flow of time around him, always searching for that elusive moment that will turn back the clock and undo Icathia's destruction.

abilities.description: Zilean stores time as Experience and can grant it to his allies. When he has enough Experience to finish an ally's level up, he can right-click them to impart it. Zilean receives as much Experience as he gives.

abilities.name: Time Bomb
abilities.description: Tosses a bomb to target area that sticks to units that come near it (prioritizes Champions). It detonates after 3 seconds, dealing area of effect damage. If a Time Bomb is detonated early by another Time Bomb, it also stuns enemies.

abilities.name: Rewind
abilities.description: Zilean can prepare himself for future confrontations, reducing the cooldowns of his other basic abilities.

abilities.name: Time Warp
abilities.description: Zilean bends time around any unit, decreasing an enemy's Move Speed or increasing an ally's Move Speed for a short time.

abilities.name: Chronoshift
abilities.description: Zilean places a protective time rune on an allied champion, teleporting the champion back in time if they take lethal damage.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Time Bomb is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Zilean's support pressure.
Use Rewind as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Time Warp or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Summon Aery is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Zilean does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Time Bomb and Time Warp only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Chronoshift should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 550 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Zilean can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Zilean's passive, Time In A Bottle, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Zilean cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Chronoshift sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Zilean wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Zilean tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Zilean should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Zilean wants to fight from.
If 51 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Zilean's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Zilean can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Dream Maker -> Redemption -> Locket of the Iron Solari is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Zilean's teamfight rating is 62/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Zilean should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Zilean, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Zilean needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from grouped fights, controlled objective zones, and cooldown layering.
Monitor Zilean's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Zilean's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.name: Zoe
champions.title: the Aspect of Twilight
champions.blurb: As the embodiment of mischief, imagination, and change, Zoe acts as the cosmic messenger of Targon, heralding major events that reshape worlds. Her mere presence warps the arcane mathematics governing realities, sometimes causing cataclysms without...
champions.lore: As the embodiment of mischief, imagination, and change, Zoe acts as the cosmic messenger of Targon, heralding major events that reshape worlds. Her mere presence warps the arcane mathematics governing realities, sometimes causing cataclysms without conscious effort or malice. This perhaps explains the breezy nonchalance with which Zoe approaches her duties, giving her plenty of time to focus on playing games, tricking mortals, or otherwise amusing herself. An encounter with Zoe can be joyous and life affirming, but it is always more than it appears and often extremely dangerous.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Paddle Star! is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Zoe's mid pressure.
Use Spell Thief as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Sleepy Trouble Bubble or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Arcane Comet is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Zoe does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Paddle Star! and Sleepy Trouble Bubble only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Portal Jump should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 550 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Zoe can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Zoe's passive, More Sparkles!, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Zoe cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Portal Jump sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Zoe wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Zoe tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Zoe should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Zoe wants to fight from.
If 50 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Zoe's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Zoe can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Stormsurge -> Rabadon's Deathcap is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Zoe's teamfight rating is 50/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Zoe should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Zoe, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Zoe needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Zoe's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Zoe's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.

champions.title: Rise of the Thorns
champions.blurb: Born in an ancient, sorcerous catastrophe, Zyra is the wrath of nature given form—an alluring hybrid of plant and human, kindling new life with every step. She views the many mortals of Valoran as little more than prey for her seeded progeny, and thinks...
champions.lore: Born in an ancient, sorcerous catastrophe, Zyra is the wrath of nature given form—an alluring hybrid of plant and human, kindling new life with every step. She views the many mortals of Valoran as little more than prey for her seeded progeny, and thinks nothing of slaying them with flurries of deadly spines. Though her true purpose has not been revealed, Zyra wanders the world, indulging her most primal urges to colonize, and strangle all other life from it.

abilities.name: Garden of Thorns
abilities.description: Seeds spawn around Zyra periodically, becoming faster with level. Zyra can cast Deadly Spines or Grasping Roots near seeds to grow plants, who fight for Zyra.

abilities.name: Deadly Spines
abilities.description: Thick vines spread through the ground and explode into spines, dealing magic damage to enemies within the area. If cast near a seed, Deadly Spines grows a Thorn Spitter plant, which fires at enemies from afar.

abilities.name: Rampant Growth
abilities.description: Zyra plants a seed, lasting up to 60 seconds. Deadly Spines and Grasping Roots cast near seeds will turn them into plants who fight for Zyra. Zyra can store multiple seeds at once, and killing enemies reduces Rampant Growth's recharge time.

abilities.name: Grasping Roots
abilities.description: Zyra sends forth vines through the ground to ensnare her target, dealing damage and rooting enemies they come across. If cast near a seed, Grasping Roots grows a Vine Lasher, whose short range attacks reduce enemy Move Speed.

abilities.name: Stranglethorns
abilities.description: Zyra summons a twisted thicket at her target location, dealing damage to enemies as it expands and knocking them airborne as it contracts. Plants within the thicket are enraged.

micro.title: Trading Patterns
points: Trade when Deadly Spines is available and the opponent must choose between last-hitting and dodging. That is the highest-value timing for Zyra's support pressure.
Use Rampant Growth as the trade stabilizer: hold it when the enemy engage cooldown is up, spend it when the wave position makes retaliation unlikely.
If the enemy misses their main CC or mobility spell, immediately test space with Grasping Roots or an auto attack. Small cooldown wins should become HP leads, not random all-ins.
When Arcane Comet is selected, shape trades around that rune's trigger window. Do not take even trades before the rune is ready unless the wave state is already won.

micro.title: Combo Execution
points: Open with the spell that confirms the rest of the pattern, then weave movement or an auto between casts so Zyra does not stand still during the damage window.

For burst windows, spend Deadly Spines and Grasping Roots only after the target has committed movement. For extended fights, stagger them so the second cooldown lands after the enemy exits their first response.
Stranglethorns should be treated as a fight commitment tool. Use it after the enemy has crossed a no-return threshold, or save it to punish the second champion entering the fight.

Practice flash variants by buffering the key spell input before Flash when the spell has a cast direction or windup. If the ability cannot be buffered cleanly, Flash first and cast after the cursor is already placed.

micro.title: Spacing, Tethering, and Cooldown Abuse
points: Hold the edge of 575 attack range when the wave is neutral. Step forward only as your minions are about to die so the opponent has to reveal their intention.
Track the enemy's lowest-cooldown trading spell. If it is down, Zyra can walk into a stronger tether range for roughly one minion last-hit cycle.
Against longer range, trade from brush, fog, or after a bounce wave. Against shorter range, kite backward through your minion line so their engage draws minion damage.
Mechanical wins come from preparing the cursor before the play starts: place it where the target will dodge, not where they are standing.

micro.title: Champion-Specific Mechanics
points: Zyra's passive, Garden of Thorns, should be checked before every fight. If it is unavailable, lower the expected damage or durability threshold.
Use ability buffering around crowd control carefully: queue movement after casts and avoid panic-spamming, because many lost fights happen when Zyra cancels a high-value auto or spell.
When the enemy has Flash, force them to spend it with the cheaper cooldown first. Save the more reliable spell for the follow-up, especially around river and turret angles.
Hidden interaction check: test item actives, summoner spells, and Stranglethorns sequencing in Practice Tool whenever a patch changes cast times or item effects.

macro.title: Lane Management and Wave Control
points: Levels 1-3 should be planned around matchup priority. If Zyra wins short trades, thin the wave and contest level spikes; if not, preserve HP and let the wave return.
Crash large waves before recall, roam, or objective setup. A weak crash gives the enemy a freeze; a clean crash gives Zyra tempo to move first.
When ahead, use slow pushes to create dive or plate windows. When behind, trim waves early and avoid fighting on stacked enemy minions.
The best recall timing is after a wave reaches enemy turret and before the opponent can hard shove the return wave. Spend gold before contesting the next neutral objective.

macro.title: Roams, Tempo, and Objective Setup
points: Zyra should move when the wave is crashed, the enemy is catching CS, or your jungler is entering the same quadrant. Random roams are only worth it if the lane state cannot be punished.
Before dragon, Baron, Herald, or Voidgrub fights, arrive early enough to place vision and occupy the angle Zyra wants to fight from.
If 52 objective control is the current profile, trade cross-map instead of coin-flipping late river entries.
Tempo resets matter more than small camps or one extra wave when a major objective spawns within the next minute.

macro.title: Side Lane, Grouping, and Win Conditions
points: Group when Zyra's cooldowns decide front-to-back fights or when your team has guaranteed engage. Split when Zyra can draw two champions and escape or win the duel.
If Dream Maker -> Redemption -> Locket of the Iron Solari is completed on curve, convert the spike immediately through plates, turret pressure, jungle invasion, or a forced objective setup.
When behind, stop matching the fed enemy alone. Catch waves safely, protect vision entrances, and fight only when the enemy spends a key cooldown first.
The win condition should be explicit: either create picks from fog, protect the carry, force side-lane pressure, or stack objectives. Do not drift between plans after 20 minutes.

macro.title: Teamfight Positioning and Flank Timing
points: Zyra's teamfight rating is 57/100, so decide before the fight whether your job is engage, follow-up, peel, or DPS uptime.

Front-to-back fights require patience: hit the closest legal target until a priority target enters guaranteed range. Flanks require earlier setup and control wards, not last-second walking through vision.
Track enemy Flash, cleanse, spell shields, stopwatches, and disengage ultimates. Zyra should not commit the main cooldown into the first defensive layer unless the team can follow.
After winning a fight, convert immediately: push mid wave, secure vision, take objective, then reset before the next spawn timer.

highElo.title: Challenger Build Variations
points: High elo players swap from the popular rune page to Pro Setup when lane survival or map tempo matters more than raw lane damage.
Boots are not automatic: choose the option that changes the next fight, not the option with the highest default pick rate.
Delay the third damage item when shutdown protection is the only way to keep Baron or Elder control.
If the enemy draft has no reliable access to Zyra, greed for snowball or scaling items; if they do, buy defense before the fight that decides the map.

highElo.title: Pro Matchup Notes
points: Pro lanes value wave state over solo kills. A forced bad recall is often a larger win than a low-probability dive.
Hold teleport, roam timers, or support movement until the next wave is solved. The move is only pro-level if the opponent loses something while answering it.
Against hard counters, neutralize the first two waves, call jungle pathing early, and play for the first item breakpoint instead of ego-trading.
Against easy matchups, slow push into dive threat and deny the bounce with deep vision, because the matchup edge must become map control.

highElo.title: Patch Trend Analysis
points: Zyra needs sharper matchup discipline on patch 16.10.1; build and rune selection matter more than blind comfort.
Current value comes from lane pressure, side-lane tempo, and converting early gold before scaling drafts stabilize.
Monitor Zyra's ban rate and role popularity after every patch; sudden movement usually means item, rune, or matchup adaptation is required.
If the patch increases game length, prioritize the scaling page and defensive third item. If the patch speeds games up, prioritize early pressure and first objective tempo.

pro.title: Elite Review Checklist
points: Every replay review should mark the first missed crash, first bad recall, first objective setup error, and first fight where Zyra's main cooldown was spent on the wrong target.
Track gold difference at 15 and ask whether it came from trades, wave control, jungle interaction, or recall timing. Fix the cause, not just the death count.
Count how many fights started with vision advantage. If the answer is low, your macro issue is setup timing rather than mechanics.
Review deaths by category: spacing, cooldown tracking, tempo greed, side-lane overstay, or objective face-check. The category determines the next practice focus.
